summary: Exit-grace: temporary bridge account, device repool and return-kit logistics for departing contractor
description:
Issue summary: A six-week contractor (infra engineer) is leaving at the end of their engagement but needs a 7-day exit grace window to finish a handover. HR requests a short-lived bridge account for access to a subset of repos and CI jobs, coordinated pickup of a loaner laptop and peripherals, and confirmation on whether we must rotate KMS keys for two service accounts the contractor touched.

Impact: Operational — the contractor needs access to finalize a canary rollback plan. Security — we must avoid over-permissive bridge accounts and ensure hardware chain-of-custody. Policy question: do we permit a bridged service account with scoped repo-only access for contractors during an exit grace period, or must we use a ticketed on-call handoff without additional credentials?

Background: Contractor was onboarded via SCIM, assigned a loaner MacBook Pro and a YubiKey. They used a pair of service accounts (ci-runner-prod, model-deploy-stager) for temporary automation during the contract. HR is coordinating pickup on-site and wants IT to prepare a clean repool checklist and mark devices for reimaging and return to inventory.
steps_taken: 2026-02-15 — HR submitted departure form and requested 7-day bridge access
2026-02-16 — IT acknowledged; asked for exact repo list and CI scopes (waiting on reporter)
2026-02-17 — Inventory reconciled: loaner laptop serial ABC123, YubiKey YK-77, docking station DS-44
2026-02-18 — Ran IAM audit on service accounts; found two service principals with recent tokens issued by contractor account
investigation_notes: Repo access: contractor has push to infra/ci and read to infra/deploy; proposal to grant bridge role 'bridged-contractor-limited' scoped to specific repos and non-production CI jobs

Service accounts: ci-runner-prod shows automation tokens from contractor until 2026-02-14; model-deploy-stager used for test deploys only — recommend rotate credentials and issue new short-lived tokens for the team to complete final teardown
KMS: contractor did not create customer-managed keys, but had decrypt permissions on a small set of test keys — KMS policy review required before rotation
Hardware: loaner MacBook has local encrypted volume FileVault enabled; ensure passphrase change is requested and device is wiped during repool
comments: 2026-02-16 — Eleanor Chen (reporter): HR will provide exact repo list by 2026-02-17 morning; pickup preferred 2026-02-22.
2026-02-17 — Ravi Singh (assignee): Noted. Preparing bridge-account template and expiry policy. Question: Should bridge be timeboxed to 72 hours instead of 7 days?
2026-02-17 — Eleanor Chen: Manager requests 7 days for handover; can we implement fine-grained repo+CI restrictions and a strict expiry?
2026-02-18 — Ravi Singh: Yes — can create bridged role with policy enforced by IAM and session expiry at 168 hours. Scheduling KMS review with Security on 2026-02-19.
2026-02-19 — Security (Amara Lopez): KMS rotation recommended for model-deploy-stager; ci-runner-prod tokens should be revoked immediately and replaced with team-run ephemeral tokens.
resolution: Planned actions: 1) Create 'bridged-contractor-limited' role scoped to listed repos and non-prod CI jobs with 168-hour expiry (scheduled 2026-02-20). 2) Revoke contractor SCIM account at end of bridge window; schedule KMS rotation for model-deploy-stager on 2026-02-22. 3) Coordinate hardware pickup on 2026-02-22; reimage and repool MacBook ABC123, disable the YubiKey and mark for inventory. 4) Post-closure: update Confluence with lessons learned and add a short addendum to the bridge-account policy. Follow-up assigned to Ravi Singh and Security (Amara Lopez).
